messages:
sam_sales: Heads-up — ACME pilot seeing 429s during pre-auth step. They hit this when uploading ~1k small documents for indexing. Can ops check quota/tokens?

marie_se: Thanks for flagging. Do we have a sample request/route from them? Is it the embeddings route or chat/generate?

sam_sales: embeddings batch endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings, they send ~1k x 512-dim payloads in 5 parallel streams. Here's a snippet they shared: `curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"open-embedding-1","input":[...1000 items...]}'` — returns 429 with body `{"error":"rate limit exceeded","code":"rate_limit_per_route"}`

tina_eng: @alex_infra could be per-route token bucket kicking in. For embeddings we throttle by request rate + token budget per tenant. If they used large parallelism it can exhaust the burst window.

alex_infra: On it. Pinging console to check tenant usage. console_bot: tenant acme-corp (id: t-023f) — last 1h: 480k embed tokens, 99% of per-route burst for /v1/embeddings. Burst window resets every 60s. Current per-route cap: 100 requests/s sustained, burst 250.

marie_se: Sounds like they hit the burst. Sam, can you ask them to reduce concurrency to 4 streams for now? Also request they split into smaller batches (100 per request) while we triage.

sam_sales: I told them to pause and reduce concurrency. They're asking for temporary bump during the demo window (tomorrow). Possible?

tina_eng: We can do a temporary per-route increase for a short window. Need approval from infra and SRE — and we should log it for billing. Alex, can you apply a 4x burst bump for 2 hours?

alex_infra: I'll apply a scoped override: per-route burst -> 1000 for tenant t-023f on /v1/embeddings, window 2h. Adding annotation `poc-temp-bump/sam_sales` for audit. Deploying now.

console_bot: override applied (id: ov-789). Effective at 1756123470.

sam_sales: Amazing — sending them the green light. Also they asked why this happened and whether it's a bug. How should I explain?

tina_eng: Explain: Not a bug — protective throttling to keep noisy tenants from hogging shared capacity. Their pattern (high parallel batches) consumes burst budget quickly. Recommendations: 1) batch smaller (<=100), 2) use backoff and retry jitter, 3) use our bulk ingest helper which does adaptive pacing.

marie_se: Also mention cost implications — large bursts cost more. Offer a Dedicated plan if they need sustained throughput.

sam_sales: Shared that and they appreciated the short-term bump. Anything else to follow up on?

alex_infra: I'll monitor ov-789 and revert automatically after 2h. Also capturing metrics into the ticket. Can someone paste the link to the ingest helper docs?

marie_se: docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/embeddings/bulk-ingest (cc @sam_sales)

sam_sales: Thanks all. I'll close this thread after the demo tomorrow, will post results. :thumbsup:
